issues.body: `_workflow_job_key` bounds the job with `(?=^  \S|\Z)`. YAML comments do not participate in indentation or close a mapping, but a line such as `  # keepalive controls` satisfies that lookahead. If that comment appears after the existing `runs-on: ubuntu-latest` and before `    if: false`, the captured block still yields the expected `runs-on` and returns `None` for `if`, so the production row passes even though the whole job is disabled. The synthetic fixture only has a four-space comment and therefore does not exercise this boundary case.
issues.fix_hint: Make the job boundary ignore comment-only lines (and refuse ambiguous/duplicate matching job definitions), then add an independent synthetic case with a two-space comment between `runs-on` and `if: false`; assert that the gate is still read. Keep the positive control before the comment so this exact truncation mutant is proven red.
issues.title: A job-indented comment hides subsequent job gates

verdict.summary:
> 🤖 SPARQ agent

The prior round's `if : false` spelling defect is corrected and directly exercised. However, the replacement job-block extractor still does not follow YAML semantics: its end lookahead treats any two-space nonblank line, including a comment, as the next job. A two-space comment inserted after `runs-on` and before a job-level `if` makes both live assertions remain green (`runs-on` is seen, `if` appears absent) while GitHub still applies the gate. The marquee job-gate check therefore remains bypassable and non-vacuous only for a subset of valid formatting. This is a new major finding despite resolution of the prior one, so progress is regressing under the required scale.
